#1787. Man City MUST stop the rot, old rivals Chelsea and Leeds set for Stamford Bridge blockbuster and Mauricio Pochettino's baptism of fire: SEVEN reasons we're excited for the return of the Premier League

Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026

After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.

And what a weekend we have coming up. Old gaffers in new colours, fierce rivalries and some seminal fixtures in the context of the whole season.

With so much to look forward to this weekend, Daily Mail Sport looks over the key reasons to be excited for the return of the world's most electric league.

After a flying start to the campaign Manchester City have begun to run into serious problems under Enzo Maresca and have lost their last three Premier League games on the trot.

And after a particularly humiliating defeat away to Nottingham Forest, who hadn't scored at home before the Cityzens' visit, Maresca and his squad will be desperate for three points especially with champions Arsenal now six points clear.

City have a good opportunity to turn things around, though, as they host a Fulham side who have endured a terrible run of form against Saturday’s opponents. In fact, the Cottagers have failed to beat City in their last 20 Premier League meetings - a run stretching back 14 years.

But, as ever in the Premier League, nothing is guaranteed and Alvaro Arbeloa’s side are showing promising signs - having enjoyed an unbeaten run in their past four games.

Enzo Maresca's side started in scintillating form but have lost their last three games

Bonfire night has only just passed but don’t be surprised to see fireworks in west London on Saturday as old rivals Chelsea and Leeds do battle at Stamford Bridge.

After comfortably surviving in their returning year last season, Leeds have kicked on and have quietly emerged as a strong contender for European football. Daniel Farke’s side currently sit ninth, just two points off fifth place Chelsea.

The Blues on the other hand have endured a stuttering, frustrating start to the season. Xabi Alonso’s heralded front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have showcased their terrifying attacking prowess, but the Blues boss’ mystifying tinkering, plus inconsistent performances, has seen his side drop points against Spurs and Sunderland.

However, form will go out of the window as this rivalry - 55 years in the making - is reignited

Chelsea will be hoping for a repeat of their 6-3 win over Leeds in the league cup this season but Daniel Farke's men will not be as easy to get past in the league

After Pierre Sage’s dismal start to life in south London, the Crystal Palace board did not hang around and gave the Frenchman the boot after just five months in charge.

And the Eagles have made sure to replace him with someone who has Premier League pedigree, Thomas Frank.

Now while recent memories of the Danish gaffer are almost universally negative it is easy to forget that before his calamitous stint at Tottenham he worked wonders down in west London for Brentford.

And he has every chance of doing the same at Selhurst Park. The job will be far from easy as his new team currently sit rock bottom of the league, but considering Frank’s high pressing and wide set playstyle, Palace’s squad looks a good fit for the Dane.

His first game back will be a tough test, away to Frank Lampard’s resurgent Coventry, but Frank - and the travelling Palace contingent - will be hoping for a new manager bounce in the east Midlands.

Thomas Frank returns to London to take charge of a struggling Crystal Palace side

With City faltering and Liverpool and Chelsea failing to hit their stride, the Premier League title race is fast developing into a one-horse competition - and Mikel Arteta will not care one bit.

The Spaniard’s well-oiled machine looks near impossible to stop but as Brighton proved before the last international break, they are not infallible and are set for a tough test returning from the latest break.

The Gunners travel to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle in what promises to be another thriller.

In years past the trip up north has proved to be a banana skin for Arsenal and Arteta, losing four out of their last six games there.

However, Newcastle fans fear their side are fast becoming a fading force and the trip to the North East isn’t perhaps as intimidating as it once was. After all, the Gunners picked up a stoppage time win there last season on their way to the title.

Mikel Arteta's side are hitting their stride but face a tough test at St James' Park

The surprise package of the season has undoubtedly been Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls who are perched in second place after 10 excellent games.

They remain the only side to have beaten the champions Arsenal and are the league’s top scorers by five goals. They are efficient, fun to watch and have scored a plethora of absolute scorchers this season, but the question on everyone’s lips is: can they keep it up?

History would suggest that overperforming teams tend to settle into the pack after a fast start, and end up battling it out for a coveted spot in a lesser European competition.

But somehow this year it feels different. Brighton appear to have everything they might need to maintain this form and seriously challenge for a Champions League place.

The squad has depth and dynamism with a littany of players boasting youthful exuberance, sprinkled with the experience of the ever-reliable Lewis Dunk and the resurgent Pascal Gross. Crucially, they have a top, motivated manager hellbent on breaking the mould.

Upon return from the break Brighton travel a stubborn Hull side, for their first ever top flight meeting between the two sides.

Brighton have been truly sensational in the opening ten games but can they keep this up going into the notoriously tough winter period

It seems that after nearly 18 months at Liverpool Florian Wirtz is finally beginning to perform.

After a dismal first year in England in which he only registered nine goals and assists in 33 Premier League games the £116million man is starting to rediscover the form that earned him that valuation.

He enjoyed possibly his best performance in a red shirt just before the break, scoring and assisting in a 3-1 away win against Crystal Palace, and has taken that form into his international performances.

The attacking midfielder got one against Serbia in a routine 3-1 win as well as netting a brace in a 5-0 drubbing of the Netherlands - with one of his strikes an absolute pearler.

The Kop will hope this is the precursor to Wirtz seriously hitting form in the Premier League but the 23-year-old still has a lot to do before he repays the money Liverpool paid for him last year.

Florian Wirtz looks in the mood after a couple of excellent performances for Germany under ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp

There is no skirting around the biggest story of the international break - the psychodrama at Manchester United. The two-week break saw the Red Devils wave goodbye to Michael Carrick and say hello to Mauricio Pochettino, hoping the incoming Argentinian will inspire a much-needed turnaround.

After an emotional press conference in which he said goodbye to the US men’s national team, who he has managed for the last two years, the former Spurs and Chelsea boss is tasked with getting his new club out of the relegation places and finding some much-needed stability.

And it will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, who takes his strugglers to the Anfield cauldron on Sunday, to face a Liverpool side who will have to travel to Anfield, to face a Liverpool side already 10 points ahead.

Factor in the history and rivalry this fixture holds and we are in for a cracker on Merseyside. The smart money would be on Liverpool but as we have seen so many times before a new manager bounce can transform a team in a matter of hours.

And that is all he will have to prepare his charges for their trip to Liverpool - with the new boss landing in Manchester on Wednesday morning to begin work straightaway. Welcome back, Pochettino.

Poch is back and this time in red but he will have his work cut out for him managing a dysfunctional United side currently sat in 18th

#1785. Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies: Who has won more honours?

By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32

Liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies count 69-68 on every senior competitive honour as of November 20, 2026.

With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.

Neither club has lifted a trophy since Liverpool's 2024-25 Premier League title, which nudged the Anfield outfit back ahead of their eternal rivals.

Liverpool and Manchester United share the record for English league titles with 20 each, after the Merseysiders' 2024-25 Premier League win matched the total the Red Devils reached in 2012-13.

United are stronger in the FA Cup, with 13 wins to Liverpool's eight, and in the Community Shield, which they have won or shared 21 times against 16 for the Anfield club.

Liverpool hold the record of 10 League Cups, four more than their rivals, and they are the only one of the pair to have won the Football League Super Cup, which was played only once.

The gap opens up in Europe, where six European Cups, three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups give the Reds 13 continental trophies to United's six.

Liverpool have more trophies than Manchester United on the fullest count, one ahead, and they also lead when Community Shields are left out.

United only draw level if the 1986 Football League Super Cup is removed or shared Community Shields are discounted, and they only go ahead on a count limited to the league, FA Cup and League Cup, which they lead 39-38.

That makes the Reds the more decorated club, since they lead or are level on every method that includes European competition, and the only count that favours the Old Trafford side ignores continental silverware altogether.

United's honours board leaves out the Super Cup and so shows the rivals level, which is a fair reading, but even on that basis the Red Devils still need one more trophy to go ahead.

Opinion is split on whether the Community Shield should count as a genuine trophy, and the FA itself treats it as a friendly for disciplinary purposes, so bookings in it do not carry over into other domestic games.

The fixture has only been contested between the league champions and the FA Cup winners since 1974, and before that it was an invitational match.

Seven of United's Community Shields and three of Liverpool's came before that change, which strengthens the case for leaving the trophy out.

The Anfield club's own honours page lists 52 major men's honours, a figure that excludes both the Community Shield and the Football League Super Cup, and the Community Shield never appeared on the honours board at their old Melwood training ground either.

Counting the Football League Super Cup but not the Community Shield gives the Reds a 53-47 lead, a six-trophy cushion over the Red Devils.

The Football League Super Cup was set up after the Heysel Stadium disaster in May 1985 and the European ban on English clubs that followed, as a replacement competition for the six sides who would have played on the continent in 1985-86.

Liverpool beat Everton in a two-legged final held back until September 1986, winning 3-1 at Anfield and 4-1 at Goodison Park for a 7-2 aggregate victory.

The tournament was never played again, which is why some honours boards ignore it, and counting it or not decides whether the Merseysiders lead or the clubs are level.

A drawn Community Shield used to be shared, and Liverpool's list includes five shared editions (1964, 1965, 1977, 1986 and 1990), while United shared four (1965, 1967, 1977 and 1990).

The years 1965, 1977 and 1990 appear on both lists, and removing every shared Community Shield leaves both clubs on 64, another count where Man United can claim a tie but not a lead.

Manchester United have their strongest case at home, with 60 domestic honours to Liverpool's 55 when Community Shields and the Football League Super Cup are counted.

In the three main domestic competitions, the league, FA Cup and League Cup, the Red Devils lead 39-38 thanks to five more FA Cup wins.

Cup finals between the pair have been split evenly, as United won the 1977 FA Cup final 2-1 and the 1996 final 1-0, while the Reds won the League Cup finals of 1983 and 2003.

The 1983 final went to extra time, with Alan Kennedy and Ronnie Whelan cancelling out Norman Whiteside's opener for a 2-1 win, and Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen scored in the 2-0 win in Cardiff 20 years later.

For every result between the two clubs rather than just the silverware, our Man Utd vs. Liverpool head-to-head record covers each meeting.

Liverpool's six European Cups are more than any other British team has won and double United's three, and that record is what separates the clubs.

The Reds add three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups, while United's six European trophies are completed by a Europa League, a Cup Winners' Cup and one UEFA Super Cup.

United edge the world honours 2-1, having won the 1999 Intercontinental Cup and the 2008 Club World Cup, while the Merseysiders won the Club World Cup in 2019.

For the stories behind several of those European nights, including the 2005 final in Istanbul, our rundown of Liverpool's 10 greatest comebacks goes back through the club's most dramatic recoveries.

Manchester United's modern haul was built under Sir Alex Ferguson, who won 38 trophies in 26 years in charge between 1986 and 2013, including 13 league titles, five FA Cups and two Champions League titles.

The teams behind that run feature heavily in our ranking of Manchester United's 10 greatest ever teams, which sets the Ferguson sides against the club's earlier eras.

The latest swings came in 2023-24, when Liverpool's League Cup win put them one ahead on the full count before the Red Devils beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final to draw level again.

The Reds' 2024-25 Premier League title then put them one clear, while on the count that ignores the Super Cup the same sequence went from a tie to a United lead and back to the current tie.

Liverpool and Manchester United are both in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase, so Europe offers the biggest single swing, alongside the FA Cup, the League Cup and the next Community Shield.

One trophy for United without a reply from Anfield would level the full count, while any Liverpool success would stretch the gap to two.

Liverpool appear to have a better chance of adding to their haul in the 2026-27 campaign, with Man United out of the League Cup and having seen any faint hopes of a title challenge evaporate amidst their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

The Old Trafford side are now led by Mauricio Pochettino, who became head coach in November 2026 after Michael Carrick was sacked.

To see what the new head coach brings, our breakdown of Pochettino's record against every Premier League club shows how his past teams have fared against each top-flight side.

For a view of current strength rather than history, our ranking of the best football teams in the world shows where Liverpool sit among Europe's elite.

#1783. Virgil van Dijk contract latest: Liverpool captain makes "no idea" admission ahead of milestone appearance in Man United clash

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:10

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a new Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk said.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he has had to settle for seven wins in his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

#1781. I can understand why fans are frustrated about lack of progress under Pocognoli, admits Andy Robertson

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026

Andy Robertson says he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Monday’s heavy defeat to Switzerland marked the conclusion of a dismal Nations League campaign which saw the Belgian’s men beat only North Macedonia across six matches to finish a distant third.

After the high of qualifying for the World Cup a year ago, supporters have been brought crashing back to earth since the summer with signs of progress proving hard to come by under the new manager.

When the full-time whistle blew in St Gallen to confirm a 4-0 loss, there were audible jeers from the travelling fans.

Skipper Robertson has no issue with what he heard and knows the players have a job on their hands to turn the situation round.

‘I can understand why they’re concerned. I can understand why they’re frustrated,’ he said. ‘I can understand why the away fans didn’t really want us to go over and applaud them.

Robertson can't hide anguish after 4-0 loss on what was his record breaking 103rd cap

‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate new people into a new squad and things like that.

‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team

‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he said. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the new players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he said. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11  players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland

‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’

#1780. Werder Bremen vs Hamburger SV - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 04:57

Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.

Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.

Daniel Thioune guided Werder to safety last term after taking the helm in early February, though his sights are set much higher this time around with his team sat in a strong position upon the league's return.

Nine matches into the campaign, Die Werderaner are sixth in the Bundesliga table, where their tally of 15 points has them two clear of seventh-placed Elversberg and just three shy of RB Leipzig in fourth.

Securing European football of any variety would be a major accomplishment for Thioune, who is currently in his first top-flight role as manager, not to mention that the club last appeared on the continental stage back in the 2010-11 Champions League group stage.

However, Werder signed off for the international break with a 1-0 defeat at Stuttgart on November 7, their second loss in three matches after a 3-2 beating by Borussia Dortmund in the DFB-Pokal in late October.

In fairness to the Green-Whites, they fought back from 2-0 down against BVB thanks to a brace from Niclas Fullkrug, only to lose out to a stoppage-time free kick by Marcel Sabitzer.

Additionally, a 2-0 victory over Hoffenheim between those defeats saw the hosts maintain their unbeaten streak on home turf this season, where they will hope to record a fourth win in five outings on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Merlin Polzin's Hamburger endured a dire start to the season, conceding 12 goals without reply in their first three Bundesliga games before firing back with a run of three consecutive triumphs.

It would be fair to say that HSV's term has been defined by streaks so far, alternating between trios of defeats and wins across all competitions, and the club will be hoping to stabilise after the international break.

Polzin's side were held to a 1-1 draw by Croatia's Hajduk Split in a friendly on November 15, following up a 3-1 success against Borussia Monchengladbach that helped to distance the team from the relegation zone in the German top flight.

That victory has left Hamburger 11th in the Bundesliga table with 12 points to their name - a total that puts them level with Eintracht Frankfurt, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart up to eighth - as well as five points clear of 16th-placed Union Berlin.

Earning another win on Sunday would be keeping with HSV's pattern this term, but after seeing the visitors lose four of their five away league matches in 2026-27, fans would be forgiven for harbouring doubts.

Werder will be without strikers Keke Topp (ACL) and Salim Musah (thigh) once again as they recover from long-term injuries, though the doubts about Marco Grull's fitness after he missed training with a calf issue will be a major concern for the team.

If Grull is sidelined on Sunday, then expect to see Niclas Fullkrug supported up top by Eren Dinkci, Chuki and Justin Njinmah.

Jens Stage and Skelly Alvero are also unavailable due to respective thigh and calf injuries, while question marks remain about the readiness of fellow midfielder Senne Lynen, who has been ill over the past week, though Youri Regeer and Ludovit Reis should be on hand to form Thioune's double pivot.

Elsewhere, the versatile Mitchell Weiser is a doubt with a thigh problem and left-back Moussa N'Diaye is recovering from a groin injury, so Arthur and Olivier Deman look set to start at full-back.

As for Hamburger, they are missing centre-back Jordan Torunarigha, who has been dealing with a hip issue, but Mario Vuskovic is likely to return after getting over a minor back injury.

The visitors are lighter in midfield than ideal, with all three of Albert Sambi Lokonga (calf), Bilal Nadir (thigh) and Nicolai Remberg (ACL) sidelined, so Martin Adeline could join Miro Muheim in the centre of the park, while Albert Gronbaek operates in the number 10 role.

Centre-forward Yussuf Poulsen is also out with a calf injury, but Terem Moffi and Patson Daka will be ready to lead the line in a strike partnership on Sunday.

Hein; Arthur, Friedl, Pieper, Deman; Regeer, Reis; Dinkci, Chuki, Njinmah; Fullkrug

Heuer; Capaldo, Omari, Bornauw; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Muheim, Moller Wolfe; Gronbaek; Moffi, Daka

Werder have been exceptional on home turf this season, and they will be expecting to collect all three points once again, but the match is likely to be closer than otherwise if Grull remains sidelined.

By contrast, Hamburger have struggled on the road throughout 2026-27, and with four defeats in five away Bundesliga games so far, expect to see the visitors' overall pattern of results broken.

#1779. Kane vows to be back for ‘business end’ of Bayern’s season after ankle surgery

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Harry Kane has vowed to be back for the business end of the season after he underwent surgery on his injured ankle.

Kane sustained an ankle ligament injury during Bayern Munich's 1-1 draw with Koln on Friday.

The Ballon d'Or winner is facing several months out on the sidelines in a huge blow to Bayern, who sit second in the Bundesliga after Borussia Dortmund's win on Saturday.

Kane, though, hopes to be back in time to help Bayern when it really matters.

The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season! “Tough times don’t last, tough people do” – my guy @Edelman11 told me this one! Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut!

"The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury, but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027," said Kane, who is likely to be out for at least three months.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.

"Tough times don't last, tough people do."

Kane has plundered 41 goals in 42 games for Bayern in 2026, while netting 15 times in as many matches for England.

The 33-year-old has only missed 14 games since he joined Bayern in 2023.

Bayern won nine of those, suffering four defeats, giving them a 64.3% win ratio. However, they have won 114 of the 158 games in which Kane has featured (72.2% win ratio).

If three points were awarded for every win, then Bayern's points-per-game average with Kane comes out at 2.33, while without the England captain, it is 2.0.

Ruben Amorim sees Adrien Rabiot as key to his squad and the Frenchman is on the verge of extending his deal with AC Milan.

This season, few players have been more impactful than Rabiot and it’s not exactly a new thing. Last year, he was vital to Massimiliano Allegri and whilst his Portuguese replacement sees things much differently, he doesn’t when it comes to Rabiot. So, a renewal has been sought for a while now.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

#1774. Prediction: Manchester City vs Napoli

Desperately seeking a Champions League boost on Tuesday night, Manchester City will welcome Napoli to the Etihad.

With Europe’s elite club competition once again stealing all of the midweek attention, there are plenty of attractive Champions League betting promotions available.

Ahead of what could be a real European thriller from the Etihad, you can find all of the key Manchester City vs Napoli H2H stats here.

Starting with the hosts, putting in another concerning performance over the weekend as they marked their return from November’s international break with a downbeat 1-1 stalemate at home against Fulham, Manchester City find themselves at the heart of a public domestic nightmare. Despite enjoying a dominant start to proceedings when opening up the 2026/27 campaign, Enzo Maresca’s superstar squad have come crashing back down to earth in a remarkable fashion. In fact, Saturday’s 1-1 draw against Fulham is astonishingly the only Premier League point that Man City have registered from their previous four consecutive top-flight appearances. Likewise, despite being last seen in Champions League action clinching a rollercoaster 3-2 win away at RB Leipzig, Tuesday’s hosts have shown some glaring defensive struggles. Including a dramatic 3-1 drumming against Nottingham Forest prior to November’s fortnight interval, Maresca’s side have failed to muster a single clean sheet from any of their last nine straight matchups across all competitions.

Sustaining a knee injury last month, Manchester City will once again be without Ghanian international Antoine Semenyo here. Missing out against Fulham on Saturday lunchtime, Maresca’s camp are still sweating over the fitness of Matheus Nunes.

Despite enduring a frustrating afternoon at the Etihad on his return from November’s international break, attacking talisman Erling Haaland has registered five goals in his first three Champions League appearances and will lead the line. Settling for a spot on the bench over the weekend, record-breaking summer recruit Enzo Fernandez will be handed an immediate full recall.

As for the visitors, claiming an essential domestic boost over the weekend as they marked their return from November’s international break with a 1-0 win at home against Torino, Napoli have drastically failed to find any kind of fluidity this season. With the pressure still firmly on Max Allegri’s shoulders, the Azzurri have recorded just a trio of their previous nine appearances across all competitions. Coming under even more scrutiny earlier in the month as they slumped to a nightmare 4-1 Champions League defeat away at Porto, Napoli have also gained an unwanted reputation for their glaring issues on the road. Opening November with a 2-0 loss at the hands of historic rivals Juventus, Tuesday’s guests have lost four of their last five matchups away from the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Likewise, the former Serie A champions have mustered just a sole win outside of Campania since back on August 22nd.

Limping off after just 13 minutes against Torino on Saturday night with a suspected hamstring injury, Napoli will be without Italian midfielder Antonio Vergara here. Likewise, picking up his own respective muscle issue earlier in the month, club captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo remains on the sidelines.

Replacing Vergara in the opening exchanges on Saturday, former Manchester City icon Kevin De Bruyne should be handed an immediate full recall on his emotional return to the Etihad. Bagging what turned out to be the winner in Campania over the weekend, Scotland international Scott McTominay will play a leading role.

Putting in another concerning display over the weekend as they were eventually forced to settle for a 1-1 stalemate against Fulham, Manchester City are desperately searching for an essential boost here. Remarkably mustering just one-point from any of their previous four consecutive Premier League showdowns, Maresca’s superstar squad have also shown some rather glaring defensive struggles. However, winning their last three straight battles against Napoli by an aggregate score of 8-3, Man City will have plenty of expectations on their shoulders in midweek.

#1773. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli not feeling the heat after dismal Nations League campaign

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:40 EST, 17 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli insists he’s unconcerned about calls for his head after a dismal start to his time in charge of Scotland.

Monday’s 4-0 defeat to Switzerland confirmed that the Belgian’s side finished a distant third in their Nations League section with the only two wins in six games coming against North Macedonia.

After a decent start to the match in St Gallen, Scotland fell behind to a Lewis Ferguson own goal and the result was put beyond doubt when the Swiss scored two quick goals at the outset of the second half.

With another performance falling way short of expectations and little sign of progress, the new manager is increasingly coming under pressure.

Despite only being in charge for 13 weeks, pundits including Michael Stewart have already called on the Scottish Football Association to draw a line under Pocognoli’s reign.

Adamant that he’s not feeling the heat, though, the 39-year-old insisted: ‘I am not thinking about this. I am just looking ahead to the next camp in March and the start of the qualification.

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is confident he'll get Scotland back on track

Skipper Andy Robertson reacts at full-time to the 4-0 defeat against Switzerland

‘We have to take the most we can from the last two camps and try to build something strong for the next one. The objective is to reach the Euros in the best position possible.

‘We will have ups and downs and it was not good in terms of the score against Switzerland. But, for me as a coach, it was a good game to see us against a strong nation away from home. That’s something we have to take into the future.’

Asked how he dealt with the growing clamour for his dismissal, he replied: ‘I don’t accept this to be honest. It’s always like this when you have a bad moment, when you think about the past. But always thinking about the past is an energy taker — we have to look forward.’

The successor to Steve Clarke, Pocognoli has tried to bring in a more attacking philosophy via a 3-4-2-1 formation.

While his reluctance to adapt has also drawn widespread criticism, he claims he’s not averse to coming up with a different approach.

‘It’s possible,’ he added. ‘I did it in Monaco and we won many tough games with a back four. I also won many good games with a back three.

‘We played in the Champions League and in half of the games we played with a different shape, so it doesn’t mean that I’m not flexible. But the timeline is to do what we are trying to do now.’

Asked if the job was proving to be tougher than he anticipated, Pocognoli said: ‘No. I think we nearly had a good game. It was just the score and the aspects in the boxes. That’s where there’s disappointment.

‘It’s step by step. And we have created a lot of chances in four of the six games. And in these six games we played one of them with 10 men and another where we were not on the level at all against Slovenia.’

#1772. Saturday’s Ligue 1 predictions including Nice vs. PSG, Lille vs. Lyon

By Saikat Mandal | 21 Nov 2026 00:20

Today's Ligue 1 predictions feature a mouth-watering encounter between Nice and Paris Saint-Germain, alongside Lyon's trip to Stade Pierre-Mauroy to take on Lille.

Two of Ligue 1's form sides meet at Allianz Riviera this weekend as Nice seek to end Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak in Saturday's matchday-11 tussle.

Luis Enrique's men are chasing an eighth consecutive league victory and a 12th straight win across all competitions, while the Eaglets aim to build on a run that yielded nine points from nine before the hiatus.

Nice's resurgence deserves considerable respect, but their defensive absences present an unwelcome complication against the division's most productive attack.

PSG have not lost at Allianz Riviera since 2022 and should have enough midfield control and attacking variety to extend their winning sequence without requiring a spectacular performance.

Facing a sceptical fanbase, Didier Digard will be eager to win over the doubters at the first time of asking when Lens host Toulouse at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Saturday evening.

The two sides are level on 13 points from their opening 10 matches, with Les Sang et Or 11th in the Ligue 1 table and Les Violets one place below only on goal difference.

Lens have enjoyed plenty of success against Toulouse in recent meetings, and Digard’s arrival could give the hosts the lift they need to respond after a difficult spell.

However, their defensive frailties remain a major concern, and the visitors’ resilience on the road suggests they have more than enough about them to take something from this fixture.

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lyon's recent dominance in this fixture makes the visitors difficult to dismiss, particularly with Vicens hoping to make an immediate impression in his first match at the helm.

However, Lille's superior defensive record, unbeaten home form and greater consistency in the league should give Ancelotti's side the edge, and we expect the hosts to secure a narrow victory.

Looking to end a five-game winless run in Ligue 1, Monaco welcome Auxerre to the Stade Louis-II on Saturday evening, hoping to get their season back on track against one of the division’s most porous defences.

The hosts sit seventh in the French top flight with 16 points from their opening 10 matches, one point adrift of sixth-placed Nice and six clear of the 14th-placed visitors, who are just two points above the relegation zone.

Monaco have struggled for consistency in recent weeks, but their unbeaten home record and superior quality should give them the edge against an Auxerre side with serious defensive problems, so we are backing the hosts to claim a narrow victory.

Vitor Matos takes charge of his first game at Strasbourg on Saturday when Brest visit the Stade de la Meinau, with the hosts looking to revive their season after a disappointing run of form prior to the international break.

The Alsace hosts sit 13th in the Ligue 1 table with 10 points from as many matches, just two clear of the relegation zone and five behind this weekend's opponents, who are themselves two points adrift of sixth-placed Nice.

Matos could bring a welcome injection of energy to Strasbourg, but just two days of training are unlikely to be enough to resolve the defensive shortcomings that have plagued the hosts this season.

Brest arrive on the back of consecutive victories, leaving the visitors well placed to edge a closely contested encounter and extend their impressive record at Stade de la Meinau.

#1771. Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”

36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a new step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

Ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT

Haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

Gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime has reported that there was some trouble in the tunnel as the two sides went off for half-time. Both sets of security teams for the clubs were forced to step in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

All the stats are massively in Manchester City’s favour but the important statistic, the scoreline, remains level.

The first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee says the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

Should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly shows the referee did not properly see it.

Porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Diogo Costa CLAWS away Erling Haaland's header 🧤Man City come closest so far in Porto 👀 pic.twitter.com/KVnBHdbNlH

In probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

Veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

With it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão. Both sides then emerge from the tunnel and here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Porto: Diogo Costa; Varela, Perez, Kiwior, Alberto Costa; Rosario, Martim Fernandes, Veiga; Gomes, Silva, Pepe.Substitutes: Claudio Ramos, Joao Costa, Hwang, Sainz, Gimenez, Souza, Fofana, Cunha, Silva, L.Gomes, Moura.

Manchester City: Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi Gvardiol; Bouaddi, Fernandez, Cherki; Foden, Haaland, Semenyo.Substitutes: Bettinelli, Rulli, Anderson, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Allan, Khusanov, McAidoo, Lewis.

It has been a decent day for Phil Foden already. The City forward’s race horse, Wreck It Ronnie, won at Goodwood and set a new record in the sport. The horse named after his son defeated Najidi Storm, which was started the race with 1-33 odds. It means the favourite is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. Foden’s family also call him “Ronnie”, which is the name he gave his son.

Will Enzo Fernández live up to the price tag for Man City? 💰@DanielSturridge tells us what he thinks he'll add to Maresca's men 💪 pic.twitter.com/ZLKdrFeTmV

The referee tonight in Porto is Szymon Marciniak, which may not be a good omen considering Manchester City have been knocked out of the Champions League in the last three seasons. The Polish referee was branded a “Madridista” last year after being pictured with a Real wash bag in the dressing room. Barcelona were unhappy with this after he took charge of a clash against Inter Milan which ended in an epic defeat.

Aston Villa have held on to beat Club Brugge 3-2 and you can catch all the reaction to that game right here.

The big news here at Estádio do Dragão is that Ayyoub Bouaddi is given his full Manchester City debut, after coming off the bench in previous Premier League games. It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

#1770. Saturday's Serie A predictions including Napoli vs. Torino, Parma vs. Roma

By Seye Omidiora | 21 Nov 2026 00:20, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 00:20

Today's Serie A predictions include Napoli at home to Torino, as well as title-contending Roma travelling to Parma.

Having left for the international break on a rare low, Como will aim to resume their stellar start to the season when Cagliari visit Stadio Sinigaglia on Saturday.

Not only are the Lariani making a big impact in Europe, they have been breaking new ground in Serie A - but defeat to the champions recently slowed their charge towards the top four.

Free-flowing Como can score from all quarters, while Cagliari must head to the mainland on a run of three away defeats, in which they shipped 10 goals.

So, the hosts will resume winning ways after their setback in Milan, keeping them on the tails of Italy's top three.

Surprise Serie A leaders Lazio will welcome Lecce to Stadio Olimpico on Saturday afternoon, aiming to extend their advantage at the top.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, the Biancocelesti sit one point above reigning champions Inter Milan, while their visitors are hovering above the drop zone.

Though a fan boycott slightly negates Lazio's home advantage, they can comfortably claim a 10th league victory of the season.

Lecce's last success dates back to mid-October - against rock-bottom Udinese - and their wait for a win will go on.

Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.

Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.

Roma can pick up where they left off before the break, as a limited Parma side will struggle to match their intensity and flair.

A fourth straight win in Serie A will warm the Giallorossi up for next week's tough trip to Paris Saint-Germain.

Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.

Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.

After two defeats and one draw from their last three games, both teams will be desperate for a win.

While Napoli are hampered by injuries and appear disunited, Torino have been leaking too many goals, so more frustration could be on the cards.

#1769. Pavlovic admits he jokes about retiring with Moreira at Partizan: “He’s a fantastic guy”

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic has spoken about potentially retiring alongside Diego Moreira in the future, after a new revelation.

It’s clear that, since he’s arrived, Moreira has had a huge impact on the dressing room. In terms of quality, Mark van Bommel called him ‘crazy’, but compared him to Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, Koni De Winter repeated similar sentiments today, saying that he may be a little crazy, but he was a good character to be around and a great footballer and Milan fans can see this, too. The Belgian is already making the €50 million paid for him look like a bargain and he has plenty of room left for growth.

Speaking to SS Calcio, Pavlovic looked at his relationship with Moreira, the help from Massimiliano Allegri last season and who gave him the most difficult game in his career, as MilanPress relayed.

“Working with Allegri was beneficial for me. It’s under his guidance that I’ve made the most progress since arriving in Italy. As a central defender, I possess good speed, strength, and skill with the ball.

“I can pass the ball forward and score goals, but tactical skills have always been a weakness of mine. I only learned the basics when I joined the first team at Partizan. Given the way Italians view football, I was a bit behind the times, as their players begin to grasp certain concepts from a very young age.”

“Physically, the toughest challenge was undoubtedly against Romelu Lukaku. But also Marcus Thuram: he’s strong, quick, and very skilled with the ball at his feet. With Lautaro, however, you have to be very careful inside the penalty area: if you don’t stay close to him, he’ll score.

The bond that unites Moreira and Pavlovic…

“I didn’t even know he was Almami’s son [a former Partizan player]. He’s a fantastic guy, really smart. He knows a few bits of Serbian. I met his father during a training session. We talked about Partizan, of course. It was really nice to see him; I remember him from his time at Partizan.”

The possibility of joining Partizan at the end of his career…

“I often joke with Moreira, telling him that, at the end of our careers, we should play at least one season at Partizan. I point out that I’m three years older than him, so he’ll have to make a small sacrifice so we can get back together. He’s a truly great guy.

“There’s a fantastic atmosphere in our group. It’s a real pleasure to be part of Milan.”

#1768. Allegri’s half-time advice to Napoli: ‘Try smiling, and we might get a goal’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Massimiliano Allegri asked for his Napoli team to play with some happiness and freedom in their Serie A clash with Torino.

Scott McTominay netted the decisive goal at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where Napoli won 1-0.

It marked Napoli's first league win in three games, since they beat Monza on October 28.

Napoli had 13 shots in the first half, worth a combined 1.34 expected goals, but they could not find the breakthrough.

And Allegri explained what he asked of his players during his half-time team talk.

He told Sky Sport Italia: "The mood wasn’t right because we had so many chances, I told them at half-time to try smiling and we might get a goal.

"They did really well to win this game, while suffering against a strong opponent. Perhaps it is positive that we won under pressure, but we also should’ve done better controlling the tempo, moving the ball from one side to the other.

"The lads did very well in defending on set plays and corner kicks."

McTominay is the only central midfielder to have scored at least 25 goals across the last three seasons in the top five European leagues (since the start of 2024-25).

He has scored four goals against Torino in Serie A, and proved the difference here.

Full time #NapoliTorino 1-0 #ForzaNapoliSempre https://t.co/97wT7xGng4

— Official SSC Napoli (@en_sscnapoli) November 21, 2026

When Antonio Vergara went off injured in the first half, Allegri brought on Kevin De Bruyne and played the former Manchester City playmaker deeper, allowing McTominay to push on.

"The fun thing about this job is finding solutions. I am starting to get to know these players, I thought De Bruyne could do better as a support for the striker, but in this situation, McTominay was more useful," Allegri added.

"I just told McTominay not to be already in the position right behind [Rasmus] Hojlund, but to run into that space, as it would make him harder to mark.

"If he is already there and not mobile, then obviously he's going to be easier to control, but he started to move between the lines and did better."

Allegri has become the first coach in Serie A history to accumulate 1,100 points, but Napoli's focus now turns to a Champions League clash with Man City.

"We need to be realistic, because as I said when the fixture list was first drawn up, our Champions League qualification would be decided in the final three matches," Allegri said.

"On Tuesday we need a good performance, try to get a result, but also know that we’ve got to sort our Serie A position first."

#1767. Harry Kane injury update: England captain ruled out for "few months" after being forced off in Bayern Munich draw

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 00:27, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:37

Bayern Munich have announced England captain Harry Kane will be out for a "few months" after he sustained an ankle injury in the 1-1 draw against FC Koln.

After netting in England's 3-2 win over Spain on Sunday, Kane returned to action for Bayern in Friday's Bundesliga meeting with Koln at the Allianz Arena.

Kane was named in the starting lineup as Vincent Kompany made his return to the touchline for the first time since he collapsed while watching Bayern's second team train.

As it proved, Bayern could not have got off to a worse start as Mikey Moore put Koln in front, shortly before Kane was forced off in the 20th minute.

The Ballon d'Or winner picked up the injury in the 15th minute when he attempted to reach Michael Olise's cross.

However, Koln full-back Joel Schmied slid in to win the ball while also making contact with Kane in the process.

The 33-year-old hobbled on for a few minutes before he eventually went to ground to receive treatment.

Unable to continue, Kane was replaced by Tom Bischof, who provided the assist for Nathaniel Brown to equalise with what proved to be the final goal of the game.

Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury at the half-time interval, which compounded a disappointing evening for the reigning Bundesliga champions.

The Bavarians have since provided a swift but pessimistic update on Kane's injury status.

The statement read: "Harry Kane suffered a torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle during FC Bayern's Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Koln on Friday evening.

"This was confirmed by an examination conducted by FC Bayern's medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be sidelined for the next few months."

Bayern also revealed Olise will "receive treatment in the coming days" after sustaining a foot problem.

In line with Bayern's "few months" timeframe, Florian Plettenberg reports that Kane will be out for at least three months with the ankle problem.

However, there is an understandable caution in putting an exact timeframe on his recovery at this early stage.

Using the early three-month prediction as a guideline, Kane will miss Bayern's final four Champions League league phase matches against Lille, Slavia Prague, Manchester United and Real Betis.

Kane would also be a doubt to feature in the knockout phase playoffs if Bayern fail to secure a top-eight finish in the league phase.

In regard to the Bundesliga, he could miss the next 12 matchdays if he is out until at least February 20.

Meanwhile, England boss Thomas Tuchel will be nervously waiting to find out the exact timeframe for Kane's rehabilitation process.

If it is around three months, Kane would be back in time for England's UEFA Nations League quarter-final clash against Norway.

But if he needs longer to recover, England's greatest goalscorer would be in a race to prove his fitness in time for the two-legged clash.

The Three Lions will travel to Norway on March 27 before hosting the second leg a few days later.
